![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14220023/assets/69dbf7a007980f1f1a9c2531ad398237e22d28f329afc619e05b8372afe970d4.png)

Consider the region bounded by the curve $x={y}^{2}-2{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis (shown in the picture). Using the shell method, calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated about the $x$-axis. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(1-2y) & =0 \\ y & =0\,\text{or}\,1-2y=0 \\ y & =0\,\text{or}\,y=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{1}{2}.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/2}y({y}^{2}-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/2}({y}^{3}-2{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1/2}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y-2{\int }_{0}^{1/2}{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4}{y}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{1/2}-\frac{2}{5}{y}^{5}\,{|}_{0}^{1/2}\,) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4}(\frac{1}{16}-0)-\frac{2}{5}(\frac{1}{32}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{64}-\frac{1}{80}) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{320}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{160}\end{aligned}
$$
